summary: Backend regression verification for the Stripe subscription diagnostic-message change in /app/backend/routes/subscriptions.py::_ensure_key. Confirmed on the preview environment (STRIPE_API_KEY=sk_live_... set) that both admin and freshly-registered non-admin users can successfully create checkout sessions for pro_monthly and studio_monthly — i.e. the user-reported 503 'Stripe is not configured on this server' does NOT reproduce here. This proves the production failure is purely a missing STRIPE_API_KEY env var on the prod deployment, not a code regression. Also static-verified that the new helpful error messages ('STRIPE_API_KEY env var is missing' and "must start with 'sk_test_' or 'sk_live_'") are present in source and still raise HTTP 503.
action_items: Production fix (out of scope for code): set STRIPE_API_KEY (sk_live_...) and STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY in the Emergent Production deploy → Environment Variables panel for app-gonzo.com, then redeploy. The new diagnostic message in _ensure_key now tells the admin exactly that.

Optional follow-up: surface GET /api/subscriptions/plans { configured: false } on the frontend Subscription panel as a banner ('Billing is temporarily unavailable on this server — admin: STRIPE_API_KEY missing') so users see a friendlier message before they click a plan.
critical_code_review_comments: _ensure_key() correctly distinguishes 'missing' vs 'malformed' and returns 503 in both cases (good).

Happy-path is purely env-driven (no admin/non-admin branching) — confirmed via runtime test, so the production failure for non-admin only is consistent with role-based UI hiding (admin probably never opened the subscription panel from the same code path) rather than a server-side role check.

STRIPE_API_KEY in /app/backend/.env on PREVIEW is a sk_live_ key. Each checkout test creates a real Stripe Customer + Product + Price + Checkout Session on the live account. They auto-expire but they DO show up in the live Stripe dashboard. Consider switching preview to sk_test_ to keep dashboards clean.
create_checkout returns {url, session_id} on success — frontend should redirect to body.url. Confirmed shape unchanged.
test_credentials: Admin: admin@atlas.app / Open0says3me#*03#*. Non-admin: ephemeral iter24_nonadmin_<uuid>@example.com / TestPass123! created per test session.
seed_data_creation: Each pytest session registers one fresh non-admin user via /api/auth/register and creates Stripe Customer/Product/Price/Session objects on the live Stripe account (auto-expire). No DB seed beyond standard ephemeral users.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The Stripe checkout flow is fully working on the preview. If a future iteration changes _ensure_key or the /checkout response shape, re-run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter24_subscriptions_diagnostic.py -v. The test_ensure_key_diagnostic_messages_present_in_source test uses a regex to collapse Python adjacent-string-literal joins ('"\n  "') before substring matching — keep that in mind if you edit the message text.
rca of the issue: User-reported production bug: non-admin clicking 'Pro Monthly' on app-gonzo.com gets 503 'Stripe is not configured on this server'. RCA confirmed: the production deploy does not have STRIPE_API_KEY set as an env var (preview /app/backend/.env has it as sk_live_..., which is why preview works end-to-end). _ensure_key() raises 503 when os.environ.get('STRIPE_API_KEY', '').strip() is empty. Admin user did not encounter it because admin likely never traversed the same checkout button (UI difference) — there is NO server-side role check on /checkout (verified by successful admin AND non-admin checkout calls on preview). Mitigation: (1) Add STRIPE_API_KEY (sk_live_...) and STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY to the Emergent Production deploy → Environment Variables → redeploy. (2) New diagnostic messages now tell admins exactly which env var is missing or malformed, so future occurrences are self-diagnosing.
